nodes_add.name: Annie Besant
nodes_add.note: President of the Theosophical Society from 1907; Krishnamurti's guardian from 1910; head of the Order of the Star's sponsors.

nodes_add.name: C.W. Leadbeater
nodes_add.note: Theosophist and former Anglican curate who claimed clairvoyance; picked out Krishnamurti at Adyar in 1909 and called him Alcyone.

nodes_add.name: David Bohm
nodes_add.note: Physicist; read The First and Last Freedom c. 1959, met Krishnamurti c. 1960-61, recorded dialogues 1965-1984 (The Ending of Time, 1985).

nodes_add.name: Aldous Huxley
nodes_add.note: Novelist; met Krishnamurti in 1938 and became a close friend; encouraged and introduced The First and Last Freedom (1954).

nodes_update.name: J. Krishnamurti
nodes_update.note: Born Madanapalle (11 May 1895 per Lutyens; claims range 4 May 1895 to 25 May 1896); dissolved the Order of the Star at Ommen, 3 August 1929; died Ojai, 17 February 1986.

edges_upsert.note: Raised and educated by the Society from 1909 as the vehicle of the World Teacher; head of the Order of the Star in the East from 1911; dissolved the Order 1929 and resigned from the Society 1930.
Picked him out on the Adyar beach in spring 1909 and claimed to read his past lives as Alcyone (letters of late 1909).
Guardian by his father's letter of March 1910; kept custody after the Privy Council dismissed the father's suit, 25 May 1914.
President of the Society from 1907 to her death in 1933.
Listened to him for years, broke with him and argued against him for the rest of his life.
Close to Krishnamurti before he recorded Nisargadatta's talks.
Met about 1960-61 after Bohm read The First and Last Freedom; recorded dialogues 1965-1984; friendship strained in the 1980s per F. David Peat.

glossary.def: Krishnamurti's phrase for watching thoughts, feelings and reactions as they arise without condemning, approving or trying to change them.

A nineteenth-century movement founded by Helena Blavatsky and Henry Steel Olcott that blended Western esotericism with Hindu and Buddhist ideas and taught that all religions share a hidden core of wisdom.

j-krishnamurti: Dissolution speech 3 Aug 1929, opening day of Star Camp, Ommen, ~3000 members; 'I maintain that Truth is a pathless land, and you cannot approach it by any path whatsoever, by any religion, by any sect.'; 'The moment you follow someone you cease to follow Truth.' -> https://kfoundation.org/dissolution-speech/

Masters 'only incidents' Paris 1927; Leadbeater 'Coming gone wrong' Adyar 1929; Eerde returned to van Pallandt 1931; Nitya death news by telegram at Port Said -> https://thelifeofkrishnamurti.kfa.org/timelines/timeline-1925-1934/

Birth 11 May 1895 (Lutyens), Williams range 4 May 1895-25 May 1896; 11 children, 6 survived; mother died when he was ten; Adyar January 1909; met Leadbeater April 1909; process from 17 Aug 1922; 'first most extraordinary experience' 19 Aug; 'touched compassion which heals all sorrow and suffering; it is not for myself, but for the world'; Nitya died 13 Nov 1925 aged 27; Rosalind married Rajagopal 1927; resigned TS 1930; no public talks 1940-1944; Huxley 1938; litigation began 1971, settled 1986; last talk Madras 4 Jan 1986; tape 7 Feb 1986; died 12:10 a.m. 17 Feb 1986; ashes Ojai, India, England; UN 1984 and 1985; Peter Michel 'rhetorical introductions to a monologue'; Lutyens 'almost instantaneous psychological transformation' -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiddu_Krishnamurti

Last words 'But nobody has done it. Nobody. And so that's that.' citing Lutyens, The Open Door (1988), pp. 148-49 -> https://www.kfionline.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/Journal%2025/files/basic-html/page123.html

Privy Council judgment 25 May 1914: father natural guardian, delegation revocable; order 'cannot stand'; boys in England, do not desire to return; suit dismissed with costs; Madras appellate decree 29 Oct 1913; guardianship letter 6 Mar 1910 -> https://future.indiankanoon.org/doc/1736356
Leadbeater letters: 6 Oct 1909 'Alcyone is at present a boy of 13 1/2, named Krishnamurti' -> https://theosophicalsociety.org.au/articles/coming-of-alcyone-to-adyar

Notebook begun 18 June 1961, kept about seven months; 'benediction', 'otherness', 'immensity'; process 'not to be confused with the state of consciousness' -> https://terebess.hu/keletkultinfo/krishnamurti/krishnamurtis_notebook/1975-00-00_krishnamurti's_notebook_foreword_by_mary_lutyens.html
Bohm and Saral found First and Last Freedom in Bristol library c. 1958-59; met at Wimbledon c. 1960; discussions with Einstein at Princeton -> https://kfoundation.org/?p=5570
Ending of Time: 13 dialogues 1980, eight at Ojai in April, five at Brockwood in June -> https://kfoundation.org/krishnamurti-and-david-bohm-3-cadogan-lutyens/
Bohm-Krishnamurti friendship strained, never regained earlier depth -> https://fdavidpeat.com/interviews/wie.htm
Recordings: earliest 1949, 600 full-length videos, aim of ~2,500 audio, 40 subtitle languages, free without adverts; playlist and On Freedom video IDs -> https://kfoundation.org/video/
1974 settlement approved 26 Dec 1974; deputy attorney general party; Pine Cottage returned; KFA Ojai offices and archives on settlement property -> https://inthepresenceofk.org/?p=916
May 1983 countersuit by Rajagopal and associates for breach of settlement and slander -> https://inthepresenceofk.org/?p=1638

Sloss book Bloomsbury May 1991, Addison-Wesley 1993; favourable reviews in The Times, LRB, TLS; KFA statement 1995; trustees knew of the affair from the 1970s-80s disputes; Lutyens 1996 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lives_in_the_Shadow_with_J._Krishnamurti
Affair began 1932, about 25 years; Radha born 1931; marriage 1927 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosalind_Rajagopal
Tricycle Winter 1991, Helen Tworkov; 'But it wasn't the affair that was so upsetting; it was all the lying.' -> https://tricycle.org/magazine/the-shadow-side-krishnamurti/

j-krishnamurti.mdx: custody case rewritten. The draft wrongly said there was a retrial and that the Privy Council let the boys choose. Bakewell J ruled for the father in April 1913, the Madras appellate bench upheld on 29 Oct 1913, and the Privy Council on 25 May 1914 affirmed the father's revocable natural guardianship but dismissed the suit because the boys were in England and unwilling to return (Privy Council judgment).
